text.tspan: One point per task, in units of (score − random) / (1 − random).
The diagonal is no change: above it a task improved after the model moved on, below it the task was forgotten.

tspan.tspan: The shaded box holds the tasks left below 0.25 — barely above a random policy — that still ended above 0.40,
the average final score across the four methods.
Ours puts 43 tasks there; every other method puts none.

text.tspan: Neither edge is fitted to flatter. Ours' advantage plateaus at +88 to +91 points for any left edge in [0.25, 0.55];
0.25 is the smallest value in that plateau where the baselines still have enough tasks (12) to compare against.
The 0.40 bar averages the four method means rather than pooling points, which would weight ours 3× for having three seeds.
Ours contributes 150 points: 50 tasks × 3 complete seeds; the others have one complete seed each so far, so 50 apiece.
